clue.text: Telephoned abroad, so spoke with raised voice

parts.note: to telephone someone is to call them, so telephoned means called
someone abroad is out of the country, so abroad gives out

explanation.surface: Someone rang from overseas and had to shout down a bad line.
explanation.definitionFit: To call out is to shout or cry aloud, speaking with a raised voice.

clue.text: Enclosures for animals caught over many years?

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
ages are very long periods of time

explanation.surface: Wild animals trapped long ago, now kept in pens.
explanation.definitionFit: Cages are barred enclosures in which animals are kept.

clue.text: Less quiet career, having moved to London location

indicators.note: having moved says the letters of the words before it have been shifted into new places

explanation.surface: Someone tires of a quiet working life and relocates to the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester Square is a famous square in London's West End, home of cinema premieres.

clue.text: Breeder is introduced by European fellow

parts.note: EU, the European Union, stands for European

indicators.note: is introduced by says the word is goes inside what follows

parts.note: a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A breeder is presented to the gathering by a man from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: IS goes into EUGENT, after its N.
explanation.definitionFit: A eugenist promotes selective human breeding, so the word stands loosely for a breeder.

clue.text: Old bit of lucre, principally

indicators.note: principally picks the first, principal, letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A small piece of ancient money, essentially.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the first letters of 'Old bit of lucre' spell an old coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece, an old piece of money.

clue.text: Say, pour drink, displaying camaraderie

indicators.note: Say tells us the next word is to be taken as heard aloud, not spelt

parts.note: to teem is to pour, as rain does
spirit is strong alcoholic drink such as gin or whisky

explanation.surface: Pouring a round of drinks shows good fellowship.
explanation.definitionFit: Team spirit is loyalty and comradeship within a group, which is camaraderie.

clue.text: Negotiate agreement shortly

indicators.note: shortly says the word for agreement is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a treaty is a formal agreement between states

explanation.surface: Advice to settle a deal quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat with someone is an old sense meaning to negotiate or bargain with them.

clue.text: Not hard to stroke an American bird

indicators.note: Not says the letter for hard is left out of the next word

parts.note: to stroke is to touch gently
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pet a gentle bird from the Americas softly.
explanation.definitionFit: The toucan is a large-billed bird of tropical Central and South America.

clue.text: Dish to take early in the day

definitions.meaning: to dish an opponent is to ruin or trounce them, which is what eating them for breakfast means
literally, what you have as your morning meal

explanation.surface: Something to eat first thing in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat someone for breakfast is to defeat them with ease; literally it is the first meal of the day.

clue.text: State playwright's assumed first name

definitions.meaning: one of the states of the USA
Thomas Lanier Williams wrote plays under an adopted first name, taken from a southern state

explanation.surface: The playwright admits his first name was invented.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is a US state and the pen name used by Thomas Williams, author of A Streetcar Named Desire.

clue.text: Coming to grief, when launching attack on a former actor?

definitions.meaning: British slang for being ruined, lost or killed

definitions.text: launching attack on a former actor?
definitions.meaning: to go for someone is to attack them, and Richard Burton was a famous Welsh film actor

explanation.surface: Someone meets disaster by picking a fight with a once-famous star.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'go for a burton' means to be destroyed or come to grief; read literally, it is going for (attacking) a Burton, the actor Richard Burton.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, wartime RAF slang, means to be killed or wrecked, that is, to come to grief.

clue.text: Writer? Hard to say

indicators.note: to say signals the word for hard is to be heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a stern person is hard or severe

explanation.surface: A one-word question, then a remark that the matter is difficult to put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was the eighteenth-century novelist who wrote Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: European about to tuck into lean piece of meat

indicators.note: to tuck into says one piece is tucked inside the other

parts.note: to lean is to slope
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A European diner is just about to start eating some lean meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck into' looks like eating a lean cut, but it is the insertion signal; CA for circa is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin boneless slice of meat, typically veal, beaten flat before frying.

clue.text: Very fashionable rider, nice to see jumping across river

indicators.note: across says the shuffled letters stretch round the letter for river
jumping says the letters of rider and nice leap into a new order

explanation.surface: An elegant horse rider makes a pretty sight leaping over a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a show-jumper clearing a stream; 'jumping' is really the anagram signal and 'across' says the river letter sits inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: French for last word, a dernier cri is the very latest fashion, so the height of style.

clue.text: Restaurant that is situated by unusual resort one's entered

indicators.note: situated by places the next piece right beside what came before
one's entered reads as one has entered, so the word for one's goes inside
unusual says the letters of resort are put into an unusual order

parts.note: one is I, and 's stands for is, giving IS
IE, id est, is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A restaurant near an odd resort that a visitor has just entered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the resort letters to ROTSER, and 'entered' puts the one's piece inside that, giving ROTISSER before the final two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a restaurant specialising in meat roasted on a turning spit.

clue.text: Northern town's favourite sort of treatment for special visitors?

definitions.text: sort of treatment for special visitors?

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire, England; the 's links it to what follows
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A northern English town has its preferred way of welcoming VIPs.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAR is a resort town on the coast of North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Red carpet treatment is the lavish ceremonial welcome given to important guests.

clue.text: Bird, one spotted west of British Isles

indicators.note: in an across clue west of means to the left, so the first piece comes before the rest

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
Is is the abbreviation for Isles

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher reports a sighting off the western coast of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a downcurved bill.

clue.text: Happen to store some food for tenant

indicators.note: to store says the first piece keeps the second inside it

parts.note: to occur is to happen
a pie is an item of food

explanation.surface: A lodger happens to keep a little food in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupier is the person living in a property, such as a tenant.

clue.text: Terrible display of anger by daughter

parts.note: ire is anger, wrath shown openly

explanation.surface: A daughter throws an awful tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means dreadful or terrible, as in dire consequences.

clue.text: Whole subcontinent's cast adrift a mountainous island

indicators.note: cast adrift says the letter named next is set loose and dropped from the word

parts.note: India is the subcontinent, and its possessive gives INDIAS
Crete is a mountainous Greek island

explanation.surface: The whole of India appears to be drifting off towards a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast adrift a' removes one A from INDIA'S, leaving INDIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiscrete means not divided into separate parts, so compact and whole.

clue.text: Ends up in hut down under

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ends are aims, and the plural gives the word for an aim twice over

explanation.surface: Something finishes up inside an Australian shack.
explanation.walkthrough: AIM AIM, two ends or aims, is turned round by 'up'. 'Down under' means Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: A mia-mia is an Aboriginal shelter or hut in Australia.

clue.text: Bill's carrying quantity of paper bags

indicators.note: carrying says the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a bill is an account, abbreviated AC, and the possessive adds S
a quire is a measure of paper, twenty-four or twenty-five sheets

explanation.surface: Bill is lugging a load of paper around in carrier bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' looks like a noun, but it is the verb: to bag something is to get it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bag something is to secure or obtain it, so bags is a synonym of gets hold of.

clue.text: Be galvanised by news from currency markets?

definitions.meaning: to cheer up or get moving with fresh energy
a buck is a US dollar, so a rising dollar is a buck going up

explanation.surface: Traders are spurred into action by a report from the foreign exchanges.
explanation.definitionFit: To buck up is to become livelier or pull yourself together, as if galvanised into action.

clue.text: Maybe model piece of writing, right to the end

indicators.note: to the end says the letter for right moves to the end of the word

parts.note: prose is a piece of ordinary written language

explanation.surface: An example of a model essay, put right from beginning to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks a model as only one kind of person who strikes a pose.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is someone who poses, as an artist's model does.

clue.text: Cut top off several trees for growth

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is to be cut away

parts.note: a clump is a small group of trees

explanation.surface: Lopping the crowns of some trees encourages them to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump is a swelling or growth on the body.

clue.text: To acclaim, a pusher reforms, abandoning love for drugs

indicators.note: reforms says the letters of the words before it are put into a new form
abandoning says a letter for love is left out of the pool before the rest is rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, a nil that looks like O

explanation.surface: A dealer gives up drugs and earns applause for going straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TO ACCLAIM A PUSHER, minus the O for 'love', are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharmaceuticals are medicinal drugs, the products of drug companies.

clue.text: What wafer-thin sandwiches! But rejected, as not kosher

indicators.note: rejected says the run is turned back and read the other way
sandwiches says the word wafer-thin holds the letters we want between its edges

explanation.surface: Delicate sandwiches are sent back because they break dietary law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like the food; it says AFERT sits inside 'wafer-thin', and 'rejected' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Trefa is the Yiddish term for food that is forbidden under Jewish dietary law.

clue.text: I muse about politician initially resisting ruler

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
Erato is the Greek muse of lyric poetry; about, meaning concerning, ties her to the politician who is written before her

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on a politician's early resistance to a dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muse' looks like a verb meaning ponder; it is the Muse Erato, and 'about' is only a link meaning concerning, with the politician placed before her.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperator was the Latin title of a Roman emperor or commander, so a ruler.
